scope: Consolidated common situations and final content holds for all 839 reviewed Math Academy questions.

hold_label_note: The math_academy_wrong_key bucket includes malformed source content and a convention conflict. It does not mean that all five are proven erroneous captured grading decisions. All 26 have independently confirmed specific content findings; no field-matching-only holds remain.
authority_policy: Every ready field was tied to full original prompt, complete saved worked solution, original before choices/layout and same captured version. Original options and source text remain verbatim. No unsupported independently authored key or silent Math Academy repair was used.

recurring_patterns.title: Saved solution authority and exact requested roles
recurring_patterns.explanation: Bind every answer field to its original prompt role, complete saved Math Academy solution, original before choices and the same captured field version. Wrong submissions and old candidate answers are not keys. Match prose semantically, translate quantifiers without changing order or domains, and derive the requested complete expression from the source equation chain rather than requiring a literal last-line match.
recurring_patterns.counts_note: Tags overlap; summed tag counts are not question coverage.

recurring_patterns.title: Roman labels, phantom blanks and field geometry
recurring_patterns.explanation: Restore presentation information from captured HTML without changing mathematics or options: 80 original I/II/III lists, 11 disappearing phantom MathML blank layouts, and one Jacobian select layout. Every select is checked separately in the original row, column or narrative position.

recurring_patterns.title: Complete matrices and paired eigenvalue answers
recurring_patterns.explanation: Retain nested matrix rows, all signs and entries, complete factors and ordered vector columns. Check paired diagonal/eigenvector matrices together using AP=PD, and pair complex conjugate eigenvalues with their corresponding vector signs. Regression matrices retain the original powers and intercept convention.

recurring_patterns.title: Vectors, domains, units and qualifiers
recurring_patterns.explanation: Check every vector component, scalar factor, unit, parameter interval, orientation, start point and excluded endpoint. Inverse trigonometric answers must lie in the principal range. Physical problems retain positive-root and growth/removal sign conventions; second ODE solutions must be independent.

recurring_patterns.title: Integral factors and bounds
recurring_patterns.explanation: Determine whether the blank asks for a numerator, one factor, a full integrand or a Jacobian. A factor already outside the blank is not repeated inside it. Preserve all original integration limits and parameter domains.

recurring_patterns.title: Graphs, diagrams and highlighted entries
recurring_patterns.explanation: Inspect original assets when they determine the answer: holes and filled endpoints, sign changes rather than touches, slope fields, orientation, shading, highlighted matrix entries, and ellipse radii. Local flat extrema follow the source’s non-strict definition. Correct verbal bindings through appended revisions when necessary.
recurring_patterns.counts_note: Tags overlap; summed tag counts are not question coverage.

recurring_patterns.title: Earlier complete evidence despite later source errors
recurring_patterns.explanation: A later source typo does not establish a wrong key when a complete earlier saved calculation uniquely supports an original option. Record the conflicting text and preserve the source verbatim. This includes matrix signs, units, coefficient errors, Roman labels and incidental prose.
recurring_patterns.counts_note: Tags overlap; summed tag counts are not question coverage.

recurring_patterns.title: Explicit conventions and inherited domains
recurring_patterns.explanation: Apply a clearly stated source convention where the original prompt and options admit it, with a caveat rather than silently redefining a theorem or domain. Examples include rectangular singular-value padding, non-strict extrema, formal IVP classification, closed-segment directional equality, and plane descriptions on an inherited function domain.
recurring_patterns.counts_note: Tags overlap; summed tag counts are not question coverage.

recurring_patterns.title: Equal definite integrals create option ambiguities
recurring_patterns.explanation: When the prompt asks for an equivalent integral or an equation’s missing expression, the intended pointwise integrand may be correct without being unique. Symmetry, periodic shifts and equal moments prove that other original options give the same integral. Fourteen final holds fall in this group; their mathematical equalities are proved, while the content defect is failure to specify the intended pointwise construction.
recurring_patterns.counts_note: Tags overlap; summed tag counts are not question coverage.

recurring_patterns.title: Equivalent lines, axes and algebraic expressions
recurring_patterns.explanation: Nonzero direction scaling and base-point shifts preserve a line; sign reversal and reordering preserve unoriented principal axes when no order is requested; split polynomial terms can simplify to the same expression. Check complete original options for duplicates before claiming a unique answer.

recurring_patterns.title: Wording and convention holds
recurring_patterns.explanation: An undefined proportionality coefficient, a derivative-order reading or coefficient-only treatment of an augmented matrix can conflict with the literal request. Preserve the finding as a wording/convention issue; do not turn it into an unsupported assertion that captured grading rejected a mathematically correct option.

recurring_patterns.title: Substantive domain and logical defects
recurring_patterns.explanation: Declared domains must define the object, and an asserted necessary conclusion must follow. Undefined sequence terms, singular polar endpoints, impossible real loci, and the invalid converse from one tangent overestimate to neighborhood concavity remain held; no repaired prompt or unsupported replacement key is imported.

prose.explanation: Original questionStatements OL determines I/II/III binding, normalized bullets omit labels. Evaluate every original statement and match one original subset option; restore labels from captured order.

Saved solution occasionally mislabels a Roman index in summary, while explicit checked statement texts and computations uniquely support original answer. Preserve source and record discrepancy; ready when requested answer is unambiguous.
Declared sequence domain includes an undefined term. Correct intended tail classification cannot justify importing malformed original prompt; hold contradictory_source without repairing domain.
Check both trig relation and inverse function's principal output range; ordinary reflected trig point outside that range is not an inverse-function point.
Inspect original graph's holes, filled points and unequal branches alongside saved solution; classify removable versus jump from finite one-sided limits.
Inspect original slope field and compare signs, vertical pole behavior, zero slopes and far-field limits for every listed equation.
Harmless source variable/constant/denominator typo can leave requested unique answer intact; record discrepancy and retain complete verbatim source.

Initial versus boundary value classification concerns same versus distinct locations. A formally posed IVP can lack classical solution at a singular coefficient; classification does not imply existence.

A source may formulate the directional MVT equality over a closed segment and include an endpoint. Distinguish satisfaction of that displayed equality from the usual theorem’s interior-point condition; hold genuine convention ambiguity instead of silently changing the domain.

A tangent overestimate at one base point is insufficient to force concavity throughout a neighborhood. Check necessity of a claimed conclusion rather than only verifying its familiar sufficient condition.

Rational and logarithmic level sets inherit the original function domain. Algebraic rearrangement must retain removed denominator-zero points and positive logarithm arguments; hold original options or source families that include forbidden points.

Normalized MathML can omit bordered phantom answer boxes. Inspect their exact original positions and restore the prompt boxes so every derivative variable, gradient coordinate, coefficient, Jacobian entry or matrix factor field has a visible requested role.
Conditional distribution answers must follow original table rows, columns and conditioning variable; source label typos do not justify transposing the requested variable.
Under the source’s non-strict local-extremum definition, points in a locally constant segment can count as extrema. Inspect the original graph and distinguish these points from peaks or valleys.

Original graph inspection may correct an earlier verbal field-binding description while leaving the independently supported original selection unchanged. Append a replacement with revision_reason and retain the earlier audit event.

compound.explanation: Submitted option from W capture is not an answer key; bind saved MA worked solution to original before choices.
Translate quantified statement preserving domains and quantifier order; truth coincidence does not make a different wording its translation.
Inflections require second derivative sign change, confirmed directly from original image.
Correct unique key can coexist with a prose error: tan(t) is not defined at π/2 despite opening assertion. Preserve source text.
Compound options include full D and P, not a fragment. Verify AP=PD with columns ordered to corresponding diagonal eigenvalues and retain row/column shape.
Rotation-scaling eigenvalue and vector signs must be paired; ∓ on eigenvalues corresponds to ± on imaginary vector component.
Source defines singular and diagonal matrices as square. Rectangular noninvertible matrices do not meet singular classification here.

MA grades only coefficient-block echelon form despite prompt asking augmented matrices; full augmented matrix may violate echelon pivots. Hold conflicting key, preserve stated convention and offered correct alternative.
MathML mphantom blanks disappear from normalization. Restore visible blank placeholders to their original rows and sides and bind requested order from original HTML.

Principal axes are unoriented lines; sign reversal and reordering preserve correctness unless the prompt explicitly imposes an order or orientation. Inspect all original options for duplicate valid eigenbases.

An eigenbasis does not establish existence of a real quadratic curve. Verify the requested level is attained by the quadratic form; semidefinite forms can make a positive or negative level impossible.

Review every select separately using the same original field DOM and choices. Matrix selects need original HTML row/column placement; narrative Fourier selects bind to the exact evaluated factor, regularity, function value and final sum.

For a question asking for an equivalent definite integral, compare values under substitutions and full-period shifts, not only pointwise integrands. Sign or phase changes can produce multiple correct original options.

Check that a parametric or polar path exists throughout its declared parameter domain. Undefined endpoints with divergent length are substantive source defects; an isolated finite cusp with piecewise-smooth branches remains valid.

Normalized content may retain a stray command absent from the saved state worked solution. Compare full source versions: if the mathematical statement and original choices agree, use the saved solution evidence and record the formatting discrepancy.

math.explanation: The prompt asks for a definite integral equality. Distinct offered integrands can have the same definite integral on a verified symmetric domain. Preserve intended MA pointwise integrand; hold when another original option satisfies the stated equality.
Scaling a nonzero direction or translating the base point along a line preserves the entire line for a real parameter. Multiple original equivalent lines are an actual option ambiguity.
A prompt/options in centimeters conflict with a saved solution explicitly concluding meters; do not silently convert or repair source units.

Read the complete row-reduction matrix, preserving nested rows and signs. A final standalone matrix can contain a sign typo while an intermediate reduced matrix supplies the valid original answer; consult grading evidence before treating this as a wrong key.
